production.name: production
production.description: In HSE, the production department refers to areas and teams directly involved in manufacturing, processing, or assembling products. Observations here often relate to machine operation, line safety, process hazards, and worker behaviors on the shop floor. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe practices, or process deviations impacting safety or environment.
examples: Operator bypassed machine guard during shift.
Spill of coolant observed near the assembly line.
Unlabeled chemical container found in production area.
Worker not wearing ear protection in manufacturing zone.
Conveyor belt emergency stop not functioning.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.description: The maintenance department handles the upkeep, repair, and servicing of equipment, machinery, and facilities. HSE observations here often involve lockout/tagout compliance, tool safety, working at heights, and risks during repairs or inspections. Incidents may include near misses during equipment servicing or unsafe conditions in maintenance workshops.
examples: Technician did not use lockout procedure before repair.
Oil spill left unattended in maintenance workshop.
Missing guard on grinder in maintenance area.
Improper ladder use observed during HVAC servicing.
Loose tools found on top of equipment after maintenance.

quality.name: quality
quality.description: The quality department oversees product standards, inspections, and compliance with quality protocols. In HSE, this area often intersects with safe sampling, handling of test materials, and ensuring that quality checks do not introduce hazards. Observations may include unsafe sample handling or non-compliance with inspection procedures.
examples: Sample bottles not labeled correctly in quality lab.
Inspector not wearing gloves during product testing.
Spilled reagent left on quality control bench.
Quality check area blocked by pallets.
Improper disposal of test materials observed.

logistics.name: logistics
logistics.description: The logistics department manages the movement, storage, and distribution of materials and products. HSE concerns here include vehicle safety, loading/unloading hazards, traffic management, and manual handling risks. Observations often involve forklift operations, blocked emergency exits, or unsafe stacking of goods.
examples: Forklift operated at excessive speed in loading bay.
Pallets stacked unsafely in receiving area.
Truck driver not wearing high-visibility vest.
Blocked fire exit in logistics corridor.
Manual lifting of heavy boxes without assistance.

administration.name: administration
administration.description: The administration department covers office-based staff and support functions such as HR, finance, and management. HSE observations here typically relate to office ergonomics, fire safety, slips/trips, and emergency preparedness in administrative areas. Events may include blocked evacuation routes or improper use of office equipment.
examples: Blocked emergency exit in admin office.
Loose cables causing trip hazard under desks.
Fire extinguisher missing from reception area.
Improper use of extension cords in finance office.
Unattended spill in administrative hallway.

safety.name: safety
safety.description: The safety department is responsible for implementing and monitoring health and safety policies, conducting risk assessments, and ensuring regulatory compliance. Observations here include safety audits, incident investigations, PPE compliance checks, and training activities. Events often involve identification of hazards or follow-up on corrective actions.
examples: Safety officer conducted PPE compliance inspection.
Near miss reported during safety walkthrough.
Outdated safety signage found in stairwell.
Incident investigation initiated by safety team.
Safety training session held for new employees.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description: The engineering department designs, modifies, and oversees technical systems, equipment, and processes. HSE observations here may involve design-related hazards, unsafe modifications, or risks during project work and commissioning. Events can include inadequate guarding on new equipment or unsafe temporary setups during installations.
examples: Temporary wiring installed without proper protection.
Engineering drawing did not specify safety barriers.
Unapproved modification to process line observed.
Commissioning team not following lockout procedures.
Missing handrails on newly installed platform.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: The warehouse department is responsible for storing raw materials, components, and finished goods. HSE issues here include storage safety, fire risks, manual handling, and vehicle movement within the warehouse. Observations often involve blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Aisle blocked by pallets in warehouse.
Racking damaged and not reported.
Employee lifting heavy box without assistance.
Forklift parked in emergency exit route.
Fire extinguisher obstructed by stored goods.

operations.name: operations
operations.description: The operations department oversees the day-to-day running of plant or site activities, often coordinating between production, maintenance, and other functions. HSE observations here may cover process safety, shift handovers, emergency response, and general site management. Events can include process upsets, unsafe shift practices, or operational deviations.
examples: Process upset reported during night shift operations.
Incomplete handover between operations teams.
Operator failed to follow standard operating procedure.
Emergency drill conducted by operations staff.
Unauthorized personnel found in control room.

facility_management.name: facility_management
facility_management.description: Facility management covers the upkeep, safety, and functionality of buildings, grounds, and infrastructure. HSE observations here include building maintenance, fire safety systems, environmental controls, and general housekeeping. Events may involve faulty emergency lighting, unsafe walkways, or issues with HVAC and utilities.
examples: Emergency exit lights not working in main corridor.
Wet floor sign missing after cleaning in lobby.
Blocked access to fire hose reel in facility area.
HVAC filter replacement overdue in office wing.
Broken handrail reported on facility staircase.
